To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the scales developed for perceived usefulness and perceived easiness of use were found to have good reliability and validity, and that perceived usefulness was found to have a greater effect on usage than did perceived ease of use.

(1) Perceived usefulness and ease of use are fundamental determinants of usage behavior; (2) the two scales are valid measures of these two variables, as demonstrated by their reliability, content and convergent, discriminative, and factorial validity; and (3) perceived ease of use is an antecedent variable of perceived usefulness, as demonstrated by the regression analyses.
perceived usefulness is a strong determinant of usage behavior and that ease of use is an indirect determinant of usage behavior through its influence on perceived usefulness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of perceived usefulness and perceived eas of use of information technology.
the development and validation of new measures of two key variables in the user acceptance model.
developing and validating a new set of measures for predicting user acceptance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
perceived ease of using a system is not a direct determinant of usage, but rather a precursor to the user's perceptions of the system's usefulness, which, in turn, determines usage.
perceived usefulness and perceived easy of use are the two most important variables that influence user acceptance of information technology.

the present research provides the first validated measures of the fundamental determinants of information technology acceptance, and that the results suggest that perceived usefulness may be a stronger determinant of system usage than is perceived ease of use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
perceived usefulness is the most significant determinant of usage, and perceived ease of user is an important antecedent of perceived usefulness.
perceived usefulness is a more important determinant of user acceptance and usage than is perceived ease of use.
the scales we developed and validated for measuring perceived usefulness and perceived easiness of use of information systems have been found to be reliable, valid, and predictive of user acceptance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
perceived ease of using and usefulness are the most important factors in predicting user acceptance of IT systems.
